subject.title: tools.loopDetection.enabled should default to true — 2 burned in 1h unguarded OAuth loop

question: Should loop detection become the default safety policy for new and upgraded installations, and if so should existing user configuration remain authoritative without adding the proposed reset behavior in the same change?
rationale: This is a compatibility-sensitive default change with a broad behavioral effect; the report supports operator cost impact but does not establish the intended upgrade contract or whether the reset proposal is safe.

options.title: Decide the default separately
options.body: Confirm the desired default and preserve explicit user settings, then land a focused source/docs/test change with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep opt-in enforcement
options.body: Retain the current default and pursue a visible diagnostic or doctor guidance path for operators who have not enabled protection.

options.title: Adopt a broader detector redesign
options.body: Treat reset semantics and default policy as one explicit design proposal with a defined progress contract before implementation.

recommendation.title: Decide the default separately
recommendation.body: Confirm the desired default and preserve explicit user settings, then land a focused source/docs/test change with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter is the only directly evidenced contact for the current production trace; a repository owner should make the final product decision after the trace is supplied.
